note: Applying phenomenology to design as a medium of meaning formation; an evolution of post-phenomenology whose next step is grounded in design thinking.
Wendt-says: not terribly different from post-phenomenology; simply an evolution that pushes classical phenomenology into the realm of design.
Chapter epigraph framing: design relates to and possibly changes the constituents of experience; addresses present and future of experience.
Theory-informed practice; cyclical theory<->practice relation where the process matters as much as the result.
Wendt-says: the walls between academia/industry and theory/practice are detrimental and counterintuitive; goals are wrapped up in one another.
Being-in as being-involved; care/concern carries over to how Dasein uses designed objects.
Designers must always work around the care with which humans interact with their world.
Personas decontextualize; a persona does not experience anything (humans do); they reinforce Cartesian dualism and represent detached understanding.
Aim is not to replace old practices but to point out their limitations; how designers frame practices makes all the difference.
Understanding systems of things and how humans experience them; experience design always has an object.
Heideggerian object-relations as a continuum, not exclusive categories; constant back-and-forth movement (keyboard example).
Invisibility/intuition/readiness-to-hand cannot stand as design goals; judged good/bad only by context of use.
Four relations (embodied, hermeneutic, alterity, background) none qualitatively superior; later the telescope figure for concealment/unconcealment.
Human-technology relationship is multistable; creative misuse beats the clearest affordances.
Reframes usability testing from removing un-intuitive features to observing users' coping strategies as core insights.
Named the hermeneutic circle of design; parts to whole and whole to parts; calls for fluid play.
Waterfall's hyper-linear positivism (gather-plan-execute) mirrors the Cartesian split and leaves no room to adapt.
Design as an 'un-throwing': humans design to take an active part in the world.
Care erodes when spread thinly; complex projects need maintained specialization so designers sustain concern.
Nothing in the book is revolutionary; phenomenology explains/augments current practices rather than supplying new ones.
Design pushes into the future, using knowledge of the past via abduction; analytical and creative thinking with equal importance.
Key design movement enacted in ethnographic research that disturbs hyper-familiar bias (terminal-patient caregiver example).
Macro/micro foreground-background movement in diagramming; the designer decides when to conceal and unconceal.
Statement 1: use documents (personas, diagrams) as thinking aids not deliverables; real value is understanding from thinking through the object.
Statement 2: new end-goals emerge in use; praxis generates theory through practical outputs (swim-lesson example).
Statement 3: subordinate intent to adaptability; launch is a step toward understanding; design with multistability for serendipity.
Theory of mediation: users adopt devices as interpretive objects; objects affect users as much as users affect objects.
Wendt-says (via Verbeek): weapons/machines/devices mediate to the point the user literally changes (gun example).
Hotel-key example: the weighted keychain makes the return decision, disclosing the activity/agency of objects.
The keychain decides for the guest; objects have systemic effects long after the client's check is cashed.
Statement 4: experience designers advocate not only for users but for preferable worlds; resist persuasive design / dark patterns.
Product semantics: identify and optimize opportunities for creating meaning through interaction; shifts evaluation from functionality to meaning.
Statement 5: products need not be functionally perfect; the meaning created in interaction is the ultimate concern; design with multistability.

RO-hook (provenance: anticipatory-application): praxis-as-being-in-the-world + the ready-to-hand/present-at-hand continuum map onto the chain's embodied energeia and its disruption-to-deliberation hinge.
In Conclusion: establish a base of knowledge on phenomenological philosophy others can build on; not a grand narrative redefining experience design.
